source.title: When is memorization of irrelevant training data necessary for high-accuracy learning?
source.authors: Gavin Brown; Mark Bun; V. Feldman; Adam M. Smith; Kunal Talwar

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops information-theoretic memorization results and reports synthetic-data reconstruction experiments, but it does not test the listed versions about natural-label generalization, its conditions, or generalization-gap measures.
record.gate_note: The paper’s theoretical bounds concern information encoded about training examples, not test error on natural labels. Its experiments report synthetic-task classification and singleton-recovery outcomes; these are recorded under fits_no_version because the task and measures do not match V1–V8. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves information-theoretic memorization requirements and measures reconstruction of synthetic training examples. It does not compare random versus natural labels, remove memorized examples and retrain, or test any intervention or measure named in V2–V7. Its notion of memorization concerns information about entire inputs, rather than the label memorization measured in V1 and V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the experiments but omits the central theoretical conclusion: for the constructed prediction tasks, any sufficiently accurate learner must retain substantial information about individual training inputs, including irrelevant features. The experiments complement these bounds by showing efficient black-box singleton reconstruction from logistic regression and MLP classifiers.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies synthetic hypercube cluster labeling and information leakage about training examples; it does not reproduce the natural-label generalization experiments or interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: For the MLP, classification errors are described as extremely non-monotonic over training, while attack recovery improves over time; after roughly 750 updates, the attack recovers almost 90% of singleton bits although singleton classification error is almost 100%.

fits_no_version.finding: For constructed next-symbol prediction and hypercube cluster-labeling tasks, sufficiently accurate learners must encode Ω(nd) bits specific to their training samples, including irrelevant features. Near-complete singleton memorization is proved for next-symbol prediction; the corresponding stronger cluster-labeling result is conditional on a conjecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near-optimal prediction can require storing substantial task-irrelevant information about training inputs under uncertainty about independent subpopulations.

fits_no_version.finding: Both classifiers achieve 0.0% training error. Logistic regression has 36.9% test error and 0.0% coordinate-attack recovery error; the MLP has 38.4% test error and 2.3% gradient-attack recovery error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard classifiers trained on synthetic hypercube clusters can encode singleton inputs sufficiently for simple black-box attacks to reconstruct nearly all their bits.

record.peer_reviewed: Symposium on the Theory of Computing
record.problems: The empirical results use a synthetic task rather than natural-label benchmarks. Table 1 reports averages over 20 trials without uncertainty estimates. Figure 4 discusses single training runs.
record.rows_left_out: No results from the paper’s experiments are left out. The theoretical information-complexity bounds are not rows because they do not measure the claim’s listed behaviors or conditions.

untested.parts: Matched training recipes fitting fixed random labels and generalizing on natural labels, including chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test-error changes as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout, weight decay, augmentation, and training-set-size interventions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons against other measures.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization scores versus equal-sized random removals, followed by retraining and test evaluation.

record.verdict_notes: Optimizer and width choices appear only in hyperparameter search, with no comparative results testing V2 or V4. Figure 4 additionally shows substantial input recovery before singleton classification succeeds; this also fits no listed version. No verdict-bearing results are missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under standard training.
Test-error behavior while widening beyond interpolation on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons on image or language benchmarks.
Large-batch generalization comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions on the specified classifiers and datasets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-gap measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples and retraining to measure test accuracy.
